title: Rent of no more than 20% of local income; stressed areas declared automatically
detail: A state index for each district or municipality: rent could not be higher than 20% of the area's average income (the list of 29 main measures says "no more than 20% of pay"). Stressed market areas (*zonas tensionadas*) would be declared automatically from objective indicators, without a decision by the region.
c: A cap at 20% of local income is much stricter than the current index and, in our estimate, below market prices in almost every city. In 2024 the Constitutional Court left the declaration of stressed areas to the regions (ruling 79/2024), and the programme itself says the Andalusian government does not declare them. There is a risk of lawsuits under art. 33 of the Constitution. According to the Fedea think tank, there were fewer rental ads in Catalonia after the 2024 caps.

s.t: Constitutional Court, ruling 79/2024 on the housing law (BOE)
Fedea (think tank), Apuntes 2026/15: the 2024 rent caps in Catalonia

title: Ban funds, companies and "speculative" purchases of homes
detail: Ban the purchase of homes by investment funds and commercial companies (except cooperatives and non-profits), and any "speculative" purchase. Large owners would face limits on new purchases in stressed areas.
c: A general ban on companies buying homes goes against the right to property and freedom of enterprise (art. 33 and 38 of the Constitution) and the EU's free movement of capital. "Speculative purchase" has no legal definition.

title: Large owner from 5 homes; end the tax breaks for SOCIMI
detail: Status of large owner (*gran tenedor*) from five homes across the country. End the tax breaks for SOCIMI (property investment companies) and funds. Tax rental income by price: affordable rents exempt, expensive ones taxed. Town halls could add a surcharge on the property tax (*IBI*) for tourist and investment homes, and there would be a tax on the empty homes of large owners.
c: The threshold and the SOCIMI regime can be changed by ordinary law. The Housing Law already lets regions lower the threshold to five homes in stressed areas. *IBI* is a local tax: the local finance law already allows a surcharge on empty homes and, in stressed areas, on tourist homes (changed in October 2026), but not on "investment" homes.
pos: Fewer tax incentives to hold homes as a financial asset; the duties of large owners cover more players.
neg: Families with five homes would fall under the rules for "large" owners. Some investors may stop building rental homes, which are already scarce.

s.t: Ley 12/2023 on the right to housing: large owner from 5 homes in stressed areas (BOE)
Local finance law (RDL 2/2004), art. 72: IBI surcharges on empty and tourist homes (BOE)

title: Freeze on tourist flat licences and withdrawal of existing ones
detail: No new licences in stressed areas, gradual withdrawal of existing ones and closing of illegal ones. Quotas for tourist flats.
c: As with Sumar: licences are issued by the regions and town halls, and the state has no such power. Catalonia limited licences with its own decree and the Constitutional Court rejected the challenge (ruling 64/2025), but that was a regional decision. Withdrawing existing licences would lead to compensation claims.

s.t: Constitutional Court ruling 64/2025: Catalan decree on tourist flats (BOE)

title: Income tax: lower for low incomes, much higher from €100,000
detail: Lower tax for the lowest incomes, much higher rates from €100,000 a year and fewer deductions for high incomes. Income from capital would be taxed at least as much as income from work. The programme gives no rates.
c: An ordinary law is enough, but the programme has no figures. Half of income tax (*IRPF*) is regional: Andalusia and other regions run by PP could lower their part of the scale in response.
pos: More progressivity; low earners keep more of their pay.
neg: High rates together with the regional part push high earners to move or to route income through companies. Revenue may be lower than calculated.

title: Permanent windfall taxes on banks, energy firms and food chains
detail: A permanent charge on the excess profits of banks and energy companies. A separate charge on the excess profits of large food chains while the basic shopping basket stays expensive.
c: The bank levy in Ley 7/2024 runs for only three years (2024–2026), and Congress did not approve the energy tax in January 2025. Food chains have low margins, so "excess profit" is hard to define there, and lawsuits are likely.

s.t: Ley 7/2024: 15% minimum tax and bank levy for 2024–2026 (BOE)
BOE, 23 Jan 2025: Congress did not approve RDL 10/2024 on the energy company tax

title: Pensions raised by actual inflation
detail: Pension increases guaranteed by law at real inflation (*IPC*) for all pensions.
c: Already in force: Ley 21/2021 set indexation to average inflation.
pos: Pensioners do not lose buying power.
neg: Costs rise automatically with any inflation, which leaves the budget less room.

title: A 32-hour week with the same pay
detail: In two years in large companies and in four in small and medium firms (*PYME*), with state help to reorganise work.
c: Congress rejected even 37.5 hours in September 2025. 32 hours in two to four years at the same pay raises the cost of an hour of work by 25%. In our estimate, no EU country has made this law.

s.t: Congress, BOCG 15-A-58-3: 37.5-hour bill returned to the government (10 Sep 2025)

title: Self-employed: fees on real income, zero when there is no income
detail: A fee based on real income, not on bands: very low for those who invoice little and zero when there is no net income. A reduced fee during holidays and a 100% discount during birth and care leave.
c: Fees on real income are being phased in, fully from 2032. A law can speed this up and add discounts. A zero fee leaves open how contribution years and the pension are counted.
pos: A lower entry threshold and fewer closures in bad months; leave after a birth without loss of income.
neg: Fewer contributions to Social Security and lower future pensions for the self-employed themselves; an incentive to under-declare income.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 13/2022: self-employed contributions on real income, in full from 2032 (BOE)

title: Extraordinary regularisation
detail: A regularisation in the spirit of the popular initiative *¡Regularización Ya!*; "nobody is condemned to illegality".
c: The government already carried out a regularisation in 2026, with about 1.17 million applications. It can be repeated by decree; a permanent mechanism needs an organic law.
pos: People leave informal work and pay contributions and taxes.
neg: Repeated regularisations create an expectation of the next one. Other Schengen countries may object, and the immigration offices (*extranjería*) are overloaded.

s.t: La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026: 1,174,978 regularisation applications filed

title: Health spending of at least 8% of GDP, set by law
detail: A legal minimum of 8% of GDP, and spending per resident in every region of at least the EU average. 25% of the health budget would go to primary care and 2% to public health.
c: As with Sumar: spending is now about 6.5 to 7% of GDP, and 1 to 1.5 points more is €17 to 25 billion a year. The regions do the spending, and a state law cannot set their budget.

s.t: Eurostat, gov_10a_exp: Spain's public health spending, % of GDP (2022–2024)

title: Write off Andalusia's debt and pay the "historical debt"
detail: Write off the part of the debt caused by underfunding and the *FLA* write-off, with interest of about 0%. Calculate and pay the "historical debt" (*deuda histórica*) under the second additional provision of the Statute, with an independent audit of underfunding since 2009 (the programme quotes a Fedea estimate of about €1,634 million a year).
c: In December 2025 the government sent parliament a bill to write off €83 billion of regional debt. In our estimate Andalusia is one of its main beneficiaries, but its government (PP) rejects the write-off. The Statute leaves the "historical debt" to a joint commission (additional provision 2). In our estimate the state treats it as settled by the 2009 agreement, so a recalculation would be a political bargain.
pos: Lower interest costs for Andalusia and more money for services.
neg: The debt does not disappear: it passes to the state, that is, to all taxpayers. A write-off rewards regions that borrowed more.

s.t: Finance Ministry, 9 Dec 2025: bill to write off €83,252 million of regional debt sent to parliament
Ley Orgánica 2/2007: Statute of Autonomy of Andalusia (BOE)

title: Andalusia as a historic nationality with the most self-government
detail: The highest level of autonomy, powers and funding in any constitutional reform, and an audit of how the Statute has been carried out.
c: "Historic nationality" is already in the 2007 Statute (art. 1). The promise is a position for a possible future reform, with no mechanism or deadline.

s.t: Ley Orgánica 2/2007: Statute of Autonomy of Andalusia (BOE)

title: A public energy company; take back grids and large power plants
detail: "Deprivatisation of all energy": a public renewable energy company with an Andalusian branch that produces, distributes and sells electricity at a fair price, and grids and large power plants returned to public hands.
c: A public company can be created (hydro concessions return to the state as they expire). In our estimate, buying out the grids and large plants would cost tens of billions of euros, with compensation required by art. 33.3 of the Constitution, and the state owns only 20% of Redeia. Taking them without a market price would be unconstitutional, but the programme does not propose that. The obstacle is money.
